answer: An applicant proves it has synced a light client by submitting a zero-knowledge proof that a chain of block headers is valid and consecutive, without revealing the headers. The chain is a ferrous spine of hashes, each pointing to the last. An anchor of the finalized tip is committed in the proof, and the tide of the chain advances one header at a time, so the proof is cheap to verify but expensive to fake, and bound to one key, so one sync buys one identity.
